_comment_purpose: ServiceNow → UI schema mapping. This is the ONLY file to edit when the target Databricks/ServiceNow schema differs from the current one. The UI layer never reads source field names — it only consumes the canonical fields defined in src/lib/servicenow/types.ts. The adapter (src/lib/servicenow/adapter.ts) uses this file to translate source rows into canonical rows.
_comment_how_to_use: 1) Update `source.catalog` / `source.schema` / `source.tables` to point at the new Databricks tables. 2) Under `fieldMappings.<canonicalField>` set the source column name (or a SQL expression) that produces the canonical value. 3) Under `valueMappings` add any enum/code → label translations (e.g. ServiceNow stores priority as integer codes 1..4). 4) Re-deploy the edge function — no UI code changes required.

source._comment: Physical location of the ServiceNow data in Databricks.

fieldMappings._comment: LEFT side = canonical UI field name (do not rename). RIGHT side = source column name OR a raw SQL expression evaluated against the source table. Use a plain column name when the source already matches; use a SQL expression (e.g. "COALESCE(short_desc, description)") when transformation is needed.

valueMappings._comment: Translate source enum codes to canonical UI labels. ServiceNow commonly stores priority/state/impact/urgency as integer codes. Add entries here when the target instance uses codes instead of labels. Empty object = pass-through (no translation).

filters._comment: Optional WHERE-clause fragments injected into each query (e.g. tenant scoping). Leave blank for none.

computed._comment: Hints used by the query builder when source column names differ. Override only if the target schema uses non-standard names for these well-known fields.
